Solar Words, Straight #1: true-up. The word installers say fast (Hawaiian Electric's tariff calls it the reconciliation), and why it matters for the credits you earn. Sources on the last slide.

Follow for more plain-English Oʻahu solar math.

#Oahu #HawaiiSolar #SolarPower #HawaiianElectric #Honolulu

slides.text: Your installer said “true-up.” Here's what it can cost you.
True-up = the once-a-year settle-up on your solar credits.
slides.sub: HECO's Rule 32 calls it the reconciliation. It's every 12 months from your own agreement start, not one date for everyone.

slides.text: All year, extra solar earns credits on your bill.
slides.sub: Credits you don't use bank forward to next month.

slides.text: At reconciliation, leftover credits go to zero.
slides.sub: Rule 32 may first turn part of them into a one-time bill credit. The rest is gone.
“How many credits will I bank a year, and how many will go to zero at reconciliation?”

slides.text: Follow for straight answers on Oʻahu solar.

items: Hawaiian Electric Rule 32, Export Rider (Sheets 49.40-J, K): banked credits carry forward; reconciliation every 12 months from the Interconnection Agreement start (Reconciliation Bill Credit); remaining banked kWh credits are set to zero.
